touches.text: Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.

Test tiers. Akien 2026-11-13, from Silicon Spice around 2000: commit, hourly, daily and weekly tests. The complete compiler test ran 40 hours across two executors, so it ran weekly, and the tiers below it meant commit time needed only smoke tests.

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. Akien: "being put in service only requires that it's the best we can do now. only requires 80% trust."

Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."
Weekly: what is too long or too host-bound to run daily, such as hollow re-runs of every proof and each box's own run of the proofs it can run.

The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.
